name: City of Cuzco
description: Cuzco sits high in the southern Peruvian Andes, at about 3,400 metres, and was once the capital of the Inca Empire. When the Spanish took over in the 16th century, they kept the Inca street plan and stonework but raised Baroque churches and palaces on top of the old foundations. Today you can walk past Inca walls supporting colonial façades, and the city is the usual gateway to Machu Picchu.
